section: Nicotinic acid as a novel inhibitor for alkaline cobalt CMP: Experiment and molecular simulation > GRAPHICALABSTRACT
text: The major mechanism of corrosion inhibition effect by nicotinic acid (NA) is to form a passivation film which adsorbs on cobalt (Co) surface so as to strengthen the surface impedance and isolate the corrosion medium. In an alkaline environment (pH 10), NA exists in the form of Nic 2− ions, which are negatively charged. Driven by electrostatic forces and Van der Waals forces between NA molecule (N atom and the carboxyl) and cobalt atom, Nic 2− ions are appealed to the Co(OH) 2, leading to the appearance of Co(II)-NA molecule groups.
